resources.string: Transmitted light from a fictional beam
Path length in the model layer

Cone photoreceptors convert light into changes in their electrical signals, a process called phototransduction. Melanin in cells of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) absorbs stray light and reduces internal reflections. These are distinct roles. The plot shows only absorption of a fictional beam by an invented, uniform layer, with all values in arbitrary model units. It does not model either cell type, retinal sensitivity, or macular pigment optical density.

The beam starts with 100 model light units. For a path length d and an absorption coefficient k, the transmitted amount is 100 × exp(−k × d). At a fixed coefficient, each equal stretch of the path absorbs the same fraction of the light entering that stretch. With no reflection or scattering in this model, the absorbed amount is 100 minus the transmitted amount.
